headlines.title: Stocks making the biggest moves Monday: L3Harris, Nvidia, Take-Two Interactive, Yeti, American Airlines & more
headlines.summary: Follow along as CNBC highlights the biggest stock market moves of the day.
headlines.article_text: Stocks moving the most today: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Visual China Group | Getty Images Nvidia shares were under pressure once again on Monday, with traders bracing for the company's quarterly report due postmarket Tuesday. Other stocks making moves include Take-Two Interactive, as gamers await the release of "Grand Theft Auto VI", and Yeti Holdings, which pulled back following an analyst downgrade. Follow along as CNBC highlights the biggest stock market moves of the day. 11 Min Ago Tyson Foods rallies on earnings beat Shares of Tyson Foods advanced more than 9% on better-than-expected quarterly results. The company delivered earnings per share of 61 cents on revenue of $14.59 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet expected a profit of 53 cents per share on revenue of $14.1 billion. Tyson is known for its portfolio of food products which include beef, pork, chicken, and prepared foods. To be sure, the company's guidance for fiscal 2027 was cause for some pause. Management expects operating income of $1.7 billion to $2.15 billion, which is in line with FactSet's $2.13 billion estimate. The company also expects beef production to decrease by about 2% next year and anticipates an operating income loss in the segment. — Paulina Likos 2 Hours Ago L3Harris drops 4% after U.S. blames contractor for Friday's nationwide groundstop The New York Stock Exchange welcomes L3Harris Technologies on April 23rd, 2026. NYSE L3Harris , a defense electronics contractor, fell 4% after the Trump administration blamed it for Friday's nearly five-hour nationwide groundstop of all airline traffic. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on Saturday said the ground stop occurred while L3Harris was performing routine maintenance. "This was an FAA system that didn't meet the moment," Duffy said at a press conference. Cancelation rates for the top six U.S. airlines reached 32% Friday and 30% on Saturday, according to FlightAware data analyzed by UBS. L3Harris shares over the past five days — Ananya Chetia 2 Hours Ago Johnson & Johnson edges higher after acquiring Ollin Biosciences Shares for Johnson & Johnson gained 1.4% after the company announced it will acquire clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company Ollin Biosciences for $2.2 billion. Johnson & Johnson also announced it will receive $750 million from Blackstone Life Sciences to fully cover the Phase 3 development of OLN324, an "investigational, next-generation bispecific antibody." — Ananya Chetia 2 Hours Ago Shares for Aramark tumble over 5% following earnings Shares for Aramark fell more than 5% after the company posted fiscal fourth-quarter results that missed the expectations. The operator of cafeterias, hospital kitchens and sports stadium food stands reported adjusted earnings per share of 71 cents on revenue of $5.29 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet expected a profit of 75 cents per share on revenue of $5.03 billion. The company also expects adjusted earnings per share to increase between 20% and 25% and revenue to grow between 9% and 10% for the full year. — Ananya Chetia 3 Hours Ago Top airline shares down after Friday's nationwide ground stop of flights Passengers queue at the Southwest Airlines desk to speak with a representative at Eppley Airfield in Omaha, Neb., on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. Nikos Frazier | Omaha World-Herald | Lee Newspapers | Getty Images Shares related to airlines, including American Airlines , Delta and United Airlines were down over 1% after the Federal Aviation Administration briefly issued a nationwide ground stop on all flights on Friday, causing flight delays and travel disruptions. On Sunday, President Donald Trump blamed the Biden administration for the FAA stop. "The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster. Everything they touched turned bad," he wrote on social media. — Ananya Chetia 3 Hours Ago StoneX upgrades Stagwell to buy from hold Shares of Stagwell popped over 1% after StoneX upgraded the digital-first marketing company to buy from hold. "Our Boston-hosted NDR last wk with CEO Mark Penn left us more optimistic on Enterprise tech solutions top line and incremental margin prospects," wrote analyst Alex Lavigne. Lavigne added while its concerned Stagwell is losing small and midsize business customers, he has a positive outlook that its growing technology and other higher-margin businesses will be profitable and make up for those losses. Lavigne set Stagwell's price target to $15, implying a 33% upside from Friday's close. — Ananya Chetia 3 Hours Ago SpaceX gains slightly after successfully catching upper stage of Starship SpaceX Starship 42 returns from orbit to the launch pad on the 15th test flight from the SpaceX launch complex in Starbase, Texas, US, November 14, 2026. Joe Skipper | Reuters SpaceX gained slightly after its spacecraft was able to catch the upper stage portion of its Starship rocket from orbit . This comes after the first phase of the flight on Friday was unsuccessful, with SpaceX unable to catch and recover the rocket's booster and exploding before it fell into the Gulf of Mexico. spcx — Ananya Chetia 4 Hours Ago Yeti falls after Goldman Sachs downgrade Yeti dropped 1.3% after Goldman Sachs downgraded the beverage container manufacturer to neutral from buy. "While our checks ahead of the print pointed to a more measured backdrop, YETI's 3Q update revealed a more meaningful softening in US DTC growth momentum. In combination with our forecast for US wholesale to slow following wholesale replenishment, we now see a tougher sales backdrop ahead for the US business which we believe will limit multiple expansion for the stock," wrote analyst Brooke Roach. — Fred Imbert 4 Hours Ago Take-Two Interactive rises ahead of 'Grand Theft Auto VI' release Commuters walk past advertising billboards for the game "Grand Theft Auto VI" in a hallway at Kings Cross underground station, in central London on November 11, 2026. Henry Nicholls | Afp | Getty Images Take-Two Interactive shares were up more than 3% ahead of Thursday's release of the much-anticipated "Grand Theft Auto VI" video game. Jefferies over the weekend also reiterated its buy rating and $300 price target on Take-Two, saying "GTA VI is just the beginning." "While the launch itself is well understood, we believe the bigger opportunity is the duration of the GTA VI monetization cycle. GTA Online and an eventual PC release could provide meaningful incremental bookings into FY28, neither of which we believe is embedded in FY27 guidance. We continue to model FY27 bookings above the high end of guidance and see upside to our $10 FY28 EPS estimate as the GTA VI ecosystem scales," wrote analyst James Heaney. headlines.article_text: J&J to buy eye disease biotech Ollin Biosciences for up to $3.3 billion Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article JNJ Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Johnson & Johnson offices in Irvine, California, US, on Friday, Oct. 10, 2025. Kyle Grillot | Bloomberg | Getty Images Johnson & ⁠Johnson said on Monday it had agreed to buy Texas-based biotech Ollin Biosciences for up to $3.33 billion, ⁠expanding its pipeline of eye disease therapies. The drugmaker said it would acquire Ollin for $2.2 billion upfront, with ​the potential for ​regulatory and commercial milestone ​payments of up to about $1.13 billion. Ollin, backed by investment firms ARCH Venture Partners and Mubadala Capital, was established in 2023 to develop treatments for ⁠vision-threatening ‌diseases. Through the deal, J&J will gain access ⁠to an experimental eye disease treatment, expanding its presence in a therapeutic area where it has a limited footprint despite its large contact lens business. Ollin is developing OLN324, an ‌experimental drug to treat diabetic macular edema (DME) and wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD), two leading causes of vision loss. "OLN324 selectively targets ​two important drivers of retinal disease and has the potential to achieve stronger and more sustained disease control," said Kip Connor, vice president, ophthalmology disease area stronghold leader, Johnson & Johnson. In a ⁠recent early-stage head-to-head study, the drug showed faster and greater improvements in eye structure ‌and greater vision gains in both DME and ‌wet AMD than Roche's Vabysmo, Ollin said. Its pipeline also includes OLN102, currently in preclinical development for thyroid eye disease and Graves' disease. The biotech has said it ⁠plans to begin late-stage studies testing OLN324 in the second half ⁠of this year, and raised $330 million in June to ⁠fund the trials. The deal is expected to close before the end of 2026. J&J said it would also enter ​into a separate agreement with Blackstone ‌Life Sciences. Blackstone will pay $750 million to the drugmaker over multiple years to fund the late-stage development of OLN324 and will, in turn, be eligible to receive payments and royalties. Last week, Pfizer said Blackstone would provide up to $1.5 billion ​through 2028 to help fund the development ‌of an experimental monthly obesity treatment.
